Greenville County by the numbers

Where is Greenville County and how is it laid out?

Greenville County sits in the northwest corner of South Carolina's Upstate, against the North Carolina line. It covers 795.57 square miles, of which 785.93 are land, and the city of Greenville is both the county seat and its largest community.

The northern boundary follows the crest of the Blue Ridge Mountains, so the county reaches higher country than most of the state. The 2010 Census lists six cities: Fountain Inn, Greenville, Greer, Mauldin, Simpsonville and Travelers Rest. Fountain Inn and Greer each spill across a county line, into Laurens and Spartanburg counties.

Much of the population lives in places that are not cities at all. Taylors, Berea, Wade Hampton, Five Forks, Gantt and Slater-Marietta are census-designated places, and each has its own mix of older ranch homes, newer subdivisions and mill-era cottages.

For a seller this layout matters because a house in Travelers Rest near the mountains and a house in Mauldin near the interstate are taxed by the same county offices but sell to very different buyers.

What is the history behind Greenville County?

The state legislature created Greenville County in 1786, and the name honors General Nathanael Greene, the Revolutionary War commander of the southern campaign. The early spelling was "Greeneville."

The county grew out of the old Ninety-Six District as settlers moved into the backcountry. The census count was 6,503 in 1790 and 53,490 in 1900. By 1950 it had reached 168,152, and it has kept climbing since.

That long growth curve explains why a single county can hold homes from the 1900s, the mill villages, the postwar subdivisions and houses finished last year. Age is the first thing a cash buyer looks at when estimating repairs, and Greenville County has every age.

How big is Greenville County and what does its economy rely on?

Greenville County is the most populous county in South Carolina, with 525,534 residents in the 2020 Census and a 2025 estimate of 583,125. Its 2022 economic output was about $40.6 billion, and unemployment ran between 2.1 and 3.3 percent from 2022 to 2024.

Health care and social assistance is the largest industry by jobs, with 43,180 workers out of 292,366. Manufacturing follows with 31,693 jobs, then retail trade with 30,485.

  • Employers named for the county include Bon Secours, Charter Communications, GE Vernova, Lockheed Martin and Michelin.
  • Prisma Health, Publix, TD Bank, the Postal Service and Walmart appear on the same list.
  • These sectors are the county's biggest sources of paychecks.

The 2025 estimate shows the county still adding people.

What roads, airports and rail serve Greenville County?

Interstates 85, 185 and 385 are the main highways, with US 25, 29, 123 and 276 crossing the county as well. Many residents live along these corridors and drive to jobs elsewhere in the county.

Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport lies mostly in Spartanburg County, while Donaldson Center Airport and Greenville Downtown Airport are inside Greenville County. Amtrak serves the city at its Greenville station.

A cash buyer prices location in whatever it is, so you do not have to stage the house or wait for a buyer who likes the road.

When are Greenville County property taxes due, and what does a late bill cost?

Real property tax in Greenville County is due without penalty by January 15. Bills usually go out near the end of October, according to the county's Real Property Services calendar.

DateWhat is added
January 15Last day to pay with no penalty
January 163 percent
February 2Further 7 percent
March 17Further 5 percent plus a $15.00 execution cost

These dates match S.C. Code 12-45-180. The Tax Collector says penalties come off only when there is direct evidence of a county error.

The office is in the South Building, Suite 1100-S, and the phone is 864.467.7050. You can pay in person, by mail or online, and most payments post within three to five business days.

The county also states that the tax on a property follows the property, not the person. If you sell with the current year unpaid, the title company normally settles the balance from your proceeds.

How does selling a house change the assessment in Greenville County?

A sale is usually an assessable transfer of interest, which means the county revalues the house to a current date. Real Property Services says the 15 percent cap on increases is removed after such a transfer, and a point-of-sale reassessment uses a December 31 appraisal date for the year of the transfer.

Ownership on January 1 decides whose name is printed on the bill. If the deed changes after that date, both the old and new owners appear on that year's bill, and only the new owner appears the following year. A new assessment notice usually arrives the year after the change.

  • Owner-occupied homes get the 4 percent legal residence assessment, plus a credit that removes the school operating tax. The application must be hand-delivered or postmarked by January 15 with an original signature, and electronic filing is not accepted.
  • A buyer who will not live in the house loses that treatment, so the bill can rise sharply for the next owner.
  • The county lists a January 30 deadline for the 25 percent exemption on transfers made the previous year.

Telling your buyer about this ahead of time avoids a surprise after closing. A short call to Real Property Services at 864.467.7300 clears up anything unclear.

How do you appeal a Greenville County assessment?

You appeal in writing, and the first deadline is printed on your assessment notice. If no notice was sent, the usual deadline is January 15, or the next working day if that falls on a weekend or holiday.

The statute behind this is S.C. Code 12-60-2510, which gives 90 days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more.

  1. Mail a written objection with the tax map number, your reasons and your opinion of value. Email and fax are not accepted, and the postmark decides timeliness.
  2. A certified appraiser reviews every timely appeal, and the assessor mails the result.
  3. You have 30 days from the notice of decision to protest to the County Board of Assessment Appeals.
  4. You have 30 days after the Board's written decision to go to the Administrative Law Judge Division.

Appeals go to Real Property Services at Greenville County Square, Suite 1000. The office schedules notices for new construction and other increases in late summer or early fall.

What happens if Greenville County taxes go unpaid?

After March 17 the bill is delinquent and the Tax Collector issues an execution notice. If the bill is still unpaid 30 days after that notice is mailed, a Notice of Seizure follows by certified mail with restricted delivery.

The sale is a public auction at the Greenville Convention Center on Exposition Drive. The sale is advertised once a week for three weeks first, and the opening bid covers all delinquent tax, penalties and costs plus the current year's tax.

The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem within 12 months. Interest on the bid is 3 percent in months one to three, 6 percent in months four to six, 9 percent in months seven to nine and 12 percent in months ten to twelve. If nobody redeems, the buyer gets a tax deed that conveys only the county's interest, not a warranty deed.

Selling before the auction is often cleaner than letting the process run. A sale closes the debt through escrow, and you avoid the redemption interest.

What does it cost to record the deed in Greenville County?

Deeds are recorded at the Register of Deeds in Suite S-2100 of Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge, Monday to Friday from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm. The office asks you to arrive by 4:30 pm.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value or part of it, according to S.C. Code Title 12, Chapter 24. The statute splits that into $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. Some transfers are exempt, including a deed in lieu of foreclosure to the mortgagee and certain family partnership or trust transfers.

Your title or escrow company normally prepares the deed and pays the fee from closing funds. If you mail a deed yourself, include a cover letter with a phone number, a stamped return envelope and a check payable to Greenville County.

More questions about Greenville County, SC Property Tax Guide

When are Greenville County property taxes due?

Greenville County real property tax is due without penalty by January 15. A 3 percent penalty starts January 16, another 7 percent on February 2, and another 5 percent plus a $15.00 execution cost on March 17.

Can I sell my Greenville County house if the taxes are unpaid?

Yes. Unpaid tax follows the property, so it is paid from your sale proceeds at closing. A cash purchase can close with the balance cleared through escrow.

Who handles assessment appeals in Greenville County?

Real Property Services does, at Greenville County Square, Suite 1000, phone 864.467.7300. Objections must be in writing, and the postmark decides whether you met the deadline.

Does selling my home raise the next owner's tax bill?

Often it does. A sale is usually an assessable transfer of interest, which removes the 15 percent cap and sets a new value. The buyer also loses the 4 percent legal residence rate if the house is not their home.

How long do I have to redeem a house sold at a Greenville County tax sale?

You have 12 months from the sale. The owner, a grantee, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem by paying the taxes, penalties, costs and the stepped interest on the bid.

Horry County by the numbers

Where is Horry County and what is the Grand Strand?

Horry County is the northeast corner of South Carolina, on the Atlantic coast against the North Carolina line. It covers 1,254.73 square miles in total, of which 1,133.31 are land and 121.42 are water, and Conway is the county seat while Myrtle Beach is the largest community.

The coastal strip around Myrtle Beach is known as the Grand Strand, and the Coast RTA bus system serves the Horry County and Grand Strand area on 15 routes. Beach communities include North Myrtle Beach, Surfside Beach, Garden City, Atlantic Beach and Briarcliffe Acres, while Loris and Aynor sit inland.

Brunswick County, NCEast

The same county tax office serves a condo near the ocean and a farmhouse near Galivants Ferry, though the buyers and the risks are very different.

What is the history of Horry County?

Horry County was created from Georgetown District in 1801, when its estimated population was 550. It is named for Revolutionary War hero Peter Horry.

Rivers and swamps isolated residents for generations, and they called the place "The Independent Republic of Horry." Even in 1950 the county had only 59,820 people.

Growth since then has been steep, and the figures show why sellers here see so many changes in a short time.

Census yearPopulation

2000196,629
2010269,291

What does the Horry County economy depend on?

Tourism is the center of the local economy. Accommodation and food services employed 23.7 percent of workers in the third quarter of 2023 at an average annual wage of $29,588, and retail trade employed 18.2 percent. The county's 2022 economic output was about $18.3 billion.

  • Employers named for the county include Adidas, the City of Myrtle Beach, Coastal Carolina University, Food Lion, Hilton Grand Vacations, Publix and Walmart.
  • The county has become a destination for retirees and second-home owners.

Many Horry County properties are second homes, rentals or condos. Owners who live out of state, or who inherited a beach-area unit, often find that managing it from afar is the hard part, and that is when a quick sale makes sense.

How do you get around Horry County?

US 17, US 501, US 378, US 76 and US 701 are the main federal routes, and state routes include SC 22, SC 31, SC 90 and SC 544. Future I-73 and Future I-74 are planned corridors.

Myrtle Beach International Airport, Conway-Horry County Airport, Grand Strand Airport in North Myrtle Beach, Green Sea Airport and Twin City Airport in Loris all operate in the county. Where your house sits relative to those routes and airports is part of how a buyer values it.

How does flooding affect Horry County houses?

Flooding is a major concern in Horry County because the Waccamaw and Pee Dee rivers and the Intracoastal Waterway all run through it, and water covers about 9 percent of the county. The county's flood resilience plan says Hurricane Florence damaged more than 2,000 buildings in Horry County and closed more than 460 roads.

Florence was the third major riverine flood in four years, after Matthew and Joaquin. Bucksport, Longs, Red Bluff and Socastee are named as target communities, and Socastee has the most repetitive loss properties among them. The plan defines repetitive loss as two or more National Flood Insurance Program claims over $1,000 in ten years.

Mapping is another issue. Under the effective 1999 FEMA maps most flooded Bucksport buildings were in the minimal-risk zone, and in Socastee fewer than 20 percent of damaged buildings (96 of 565) were in the effective Special Flood Hazard Area.

If you own a flood-damaged or flood-prone house, a cash buyer who purchases as-is can take it without asking you to rebuild first.

When is Horry County property tax billed, and what are the due dates?

Horry County mails real property notices to the owner of record on October 1, and full payment is due by January 15 of the following year. Penalties take effect on January 16, February 2 and March 17, and the U.S. postmark decides whether a mailed payment is late.

The percentages are in S.C. Code 12-45-180: 3 percent, then 7 percent, then 5 percent. The county page does not list the amounts, so check your notice.

  • Treasurer phone for payments: 843-428-2126.
  • Pay at the Treasurer's Office, by mail, at a night deposit box, online or by phone. Card payments carry a convenience fee.
  • Not receiving a bill does not excuse a late payment, and the notice reflects ownership as of January 1.

Can you pay Horry County tax in installments?

Yes, for real property only, if the application is received before January 15 of the tax year. Escrowed property and personal vehicles are excluded.

The payment is the prior year's tax times 16.67 percent, made in five advance payments due February 15, April 15, June 15, August 15 and October 15. The balance is billed by November 15, and no installment is accepted after October 15.

Applications may be denied for outstanding taxes, a bank escrow account or non-ownership of the property. If you plan to sell mid-year, ask the Treasurer how the plan interacts with your closing.

How do reassessment and the legal residence rate work in Horry County?

Horry County reassesses every four years and implements in the fifth, according to its Assessor. The last was in 2019 and the next was scheduled for tax year 2024, so confirm the current cycle with the office.

Increases from a countywide reappraisal are limited to 15 percent over five years, but the cap does not apply in the year an assessable transfer of interest first becomes taxable. A sale is the usual trigger for that.

  • Legal residence, the 4 percent assessment, must be applied for between January 1 and January 15.
  • Use changes must be reported to the Assessor within six months.
  • The homestead deduction of $50,000 is for owners 65 or older, the blind, the disabled and surviving spouses, and first-time applicants apply in person at the Auditor's Office, 843-915-5051.

How do you appeal an Horry County assessment?

Request a conference in writing within 90 days of the assessment notice. In a year with no notice you can appeal at any time, and an appeal filed before the first penalty date applies to that tax year.

Your letter should include your name, the Map-Block-Parcel number, the value you think is correct and your reasons. The legal basis is S.C. Code 12-60-2510. For agricultural land that changes use, roll-back taxes apply for the year of change and four prior years.

What happens after Horry County taxes become delinquent?

Real property taxes are delinquent on March 17, and notices go out around April 1. Certified notices follow 30 days later, and levy notices are posted on delinquent properties, usually between May and October.

The sale is advertised on three consecutive Thursdays, and the redemption period is 12 months from the sale date. The Delinquent Tax Office is at 1301 Second Avenue, Conway, phone (843) 915-5472, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm. The county said the 2026 sale date and location would appear in a November newspaper ad.

State and county recording tax on the deed is $1.85 per $500 of value under Title 12, Chapter 24. We could not open the Horry County Register of Deeds page, so ask that office about its filing steps.

More questions about Horry County, SC Property Tax Guide

When are Horry County property taxes due?

Real property tax is due by January 15, and notices are mailed October 1. Penalties start on January 16, February 2 and March 17.

Does Horry County allow installment payments?

Yes, for real property if you apply before January 15. You pay 16.67 percent of last year's tax in five installments, February through October, and the balance is billed by November 15.

How do I apply for the 4 percent legal residence rate in Horry County?

File between January 1 and January 15 of the tax year. You must own and live in the home as your primary residence as of January 1.

How long can I redeem a house sold at an Horry County tax sale?

You have 12 months from the sale date. The owner, mortgage company or grantee can pay the taxes and sale costs to regain ownership.

Is Horry County property flood prone?

Parts of it are, and the county's own plan names Bucksport, Longs, Red Bluff and Socastee. Check flood zone status and insurance history before you list or sell a house.

Aiken County by the numbers

Where is Aiken County and what is in it?

Aiken County is in western South Carolina, across the Savannah River from Georgia, and is part of the Augusta-Richmond County metropolitan area. It covers 1,080.17 square miles, which makes it the fourth-largest South Carolina county by land area.

The county seat and largest community is the city of Aiken. Other cities are New Ellenton and North Augusta, which is partly in Edgefield County. The towns are Burnettown, Jackson, Perry, Salley, Monetta, Wagener and Windsor, and census-designated places include Beech Island, Graniteville, Clearwater and Warrenville.

The land runs from the Piedmont in the north through the Sandhills to the Coastal Plain in the south. It borders Saluda, Lexington, Orangeburg, Barnwell and Edgefield counties, plus Burke and Richmond counties in Georgia. A seller in a town such as Wagener faces a different market than one in North Augusta, even though both mail their tax payment to the same county.

What is the history that shapes Aiken County today?

Aiken County was organized in 1871 from parts of Barnwell, Edgefield, Lexington and Orangeburg counties. It was named for William Aiken, the first president of the South Carolina Railroad Company.

Two later events changed the map. In the late 19th century the county became a winter refuge for wealthy Northerners, who built large houses, and it remains known for horse training because the winters are mild. In the 1950s the Savannah River Site was built, which required acquiring the town of Ellenton. Its residents and businesses moved about eight miles north to New Ellenton and about five miles south to Jackson.

The county grew from 53,137 residents in 1950 to 81,038 in 1960, then reached 168,808 in 2020. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 181,515.

When are Aiken County property taxes due?

South Carolina law makes property tax payable between September 30 and January 15 after the assessment. The county treasurer collects under the Department of Revenue's supervision, and receipts must describe real estate by tax map number.

Under the penalty statute, a bill unpaid before January 16, or 30 days after the notice is mailed if that is later, picks up a 3% penalty. A further 7% is added if it remains unpaid before February 2, and another 5% before March 17. After March 17 the treasurer issues an execution to the delinquent collector. A U.S. postmark is the determining date for mailed payments.

What happens to penalties when a house changes hands?

If the title to real property moves during a tax year and the county mailed the notice to the prior owner, the treasurer shall waive the penalty when the new owner got no timely notice. This is in subsection (B) of the penalty statute.

That matters for an inherited or sold house in Aiken County. A notice sent to a deceased owner or a former owner may not reach the person who now holds the deed. Ask the treasurer to update the mailing address in the same week the deed is recorded, and keep a copy of that request in case the bill is questioned later.

How do you object to an assessment in Aiken County?

A property owner objects to the assessor in writing. The state law says that when the assessor sends an assessment notice, the owner has 90 days after the mailing to give written notice of objection to the fair market value, special use value, assessment ratio or the assessment itself.

Notices are required when the assessor raises value by $1,000 or more or makes the first assessment on a property. In years with no notice, the owner can appeal at any time in writing. An appeal filed before the first penalty date applies to that tax year, and one filed on or after that date applies to the next year. In a countywide reassessment year, substantially all notices must be mailed by October 1.

We did not open the county's assessor or appeals pages, so we do not describe the hearing steps, forms or office hours. Ask the Aiken County offices which form to use and where to file it.

Greenwood County by the numbers

Where is Greenwood County and what towns are in it?

Greenwood County is in the western Piedmont of South Carolina and covers 463.81 square miles, with 455.60 of that land. Greenwood is the county seat and the largest community.

Four other incorporated places sit in the county: Hodges, Ninety Six, Troy and Ware Shoals, and Ware Shoals reaches into Abbeville and Laurens counties. Unincorporated communities include Callison, Epworth, Kirksey, Phoenix, Pittsburg, Shoals Junction and Verdery.

A house in a small town such as Troy or Hodges sells in a very different pool of buyers than a house in the city of Greenwood, though all of them are taxed through the same courthouse.

How did Greenwood County begin?

Greenwood County was formed in 1897 from parts of Abbeville and Edgefield counties, both once part of the Ninety-Six District. It was named for its seat, and the town took its name around 1824 from a cotton plantation owned by John McGehee.

The 2020 Census counted 69,351 residents, close to the 69,661 counted in 2010. The 2025 estimate is 70,379, so the county is large enough to keep a real market but has not seen the surge some of its neighbors have.

Slow, steady population means many homes here are owned for a long time and pass through families. When an heir ends up with a house in the county that they do not plan to keep, selling for cash can be simpler than a listing.

What is Lake Greenwood and why does it matter to homeowners?

Lake Greenwood was created by the Buzzard's Roost Dam on the Saluda River, which the county page describes as the largest New Deal project in the area. The county later sold the hydroelectric plant to Duke Power Company.

The lake offers recreation for residents and visitors, and many owners near it hold second homes rather than primary residences.

The Auditor says the school-tax credit does not apply to second homes, so a lake house that is not your legal residence is billed differently from a primary home. Ask the Assessor how your parcel is classified.

What industries and employers support Greenwood County?

Health care and social assistance made up 22.1 percent of employment in the third quarter of 2023, manufacturing 19.8 percent and retail trade 12.8 percent.

  • Healthcare and education: Self Regional Healthcare, the Greenwood County school districts, Lander University and Piedmont Technical College.
  • Manufacturing: Eaton Corporation, FujiFilm, Capsugel, Ascend Performance Materials and VELUX.
  • Distribution and health products: Cardinal Health is also on the major employer list.

With a few large employers carrying much of the job base, sellers who need to relocate on a deadline often want a closing date they control.

What highways cross Greenwood County?

US 25 and US 178 are the principal federal routes, with business routes in the city of Greenwood, and US 221 also crosses the county. State routes include SC 10, 34, 72, 246, 248, 252 and 702.

Business routes run through both Greenwood and Ware Shoals, so those towns have main streets that carry through traffic. Distance from a main route is something buyers weigh, and a cash buyer prices it in without asking you to wait for the right match.

Which Greenwood County offices handle property tax?

Three offices at the Greenwood County Courthouse, 528 Monument Street, handle most of the work. Hours at each are 7:45 to 5:30, Monday through Thursday, and they are closed Friday.

OfficeRoomPhoneHandles
Assessor109(864) 942-8537Valuation and appeals
AuditorSuite 107(864) 942-8543Homestead and legal residence credit
Tax Collector101(864) 942-3142Payments, redemptions

The Assessor's staff has five licensed appraisers and four support staff. The office notes that a complaint about the amount of a tax bill cannot be an assessment appeal, since an appeal has to challenge value, use classification or ratio.

How and when do you pay Greenwood County property tax?

Advance installments on real estate are due in February, April, June, August and October, and the final payment is due on or before January 15 of the following year. The county posted this year's bills online on November 4, 2026.

  • You can pay in person, by mail, in the lobby drop box or online through the county's payment vendor.
  • Accepted forms include cash, certified checks, money orders and major credit cards, and a convenience fee may apply to cards.
  • Out-of-state checks are not accepted for delinquent real estate taxes.

The Tax Collector page does not list late penalties. The state schedule in S.C. Code 12-45-180 applies: 3 percent after January 15, a further 7 percent on February 2 and a further 5 percent on March 17. Ask the office to confirm the amount for your bill.

Who qualifies for the homestead exemption and the school-tax credit?

An owner who is 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind can apply for the homestead exemption, provided they hold fee simple title or a life estate in the primary residence. They must have been a South Carolina resident for a calendar year as of December 31 of the preceding tax year.

The Auditor says qualifying legal residents get a 4 percent homeowners credit on school operating taxes and pay only school bond taxes. That credit does not reach second homes, land or business property.

Anyone who sells or rents the home, or changes the owners on the deed, must tell the Auditor. A sale therefore ends the exemption for the seller, and the buyer must apply for their own.

What should you know about appeals and rollback taxes in Greenwood County?

If your notice raised value by $1,000 or more, you have 90 days from mailing to object in writing under S.C. Code 12-60-2510. Send the objection to the Assessor at Room 109.

Agricultural-use land needs at least 5 acres in timber or 10 acres in crops, including pasture. If the use changes, up to five years of taxes can become due, which is a real concern for a seller who is subdividing a family tract.

Builders can seek the exemption for newly built single-family homes, and subdivision lots may qualify for a multiple lot discount. Both are handled through the Assessor.

How does a deed get recorded and what if the tax goes unpaid?

The Register of Deeds is in Room 114 of the courthouse, open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, at (864) 942-8612. Documents brought in are recorded the same day, though anything after 4 p.m. waits until the next day, and originals are mailed back 3 to 5 business days later.

The recording tax is $1.85 per $500 under Title 12, Chapter 24. State tax liens are no longer filed with county offices and appear on the Department of Revenue's registry.

Tax sale redemptions are handled in Room 101 and accepted only as cash, certified check or money order, never by card. Selling before a sale avoids that route.

More questions about Greenwood County, SC Property Tax Guide

When is the final Greenwood County property tax payment due?

The final payment is due on or before January 15 of the year after the tax year. The county also offers advance installments in February, April, June, August and October.

Can I pay Greenwood County taxes online?

Yes, current and delinquent real, personal and mobile home taxes can be paid online through the county's vendor, as well as in person, by mail or in the lobby drop box. A card fee may apply.

Does Greenwood County offer a homestead exemption?

Yes, for owners 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind who meet ownership and residency rules. Apply in person with the Auditor, and notify the office if you sell or rent.

How long do I have to object to a Greenwood County assessment?

You have 90 days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more. The objection goes in writing to the Assessor.

What are the office hours for Greenwood County tax offices?

The Assessor, Auditor and Tax Collector keep 7:45 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and close Friday. The Register of Deeds is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.
